intro: This headphones icon draws over-ear headphones: a curved headband joining two padded ear cups. It signals listening, often privately, so use it for music and podcast apps, audio settings, connected Bluetooth devices, listening modes and support links where a real person is ready to talk to you.
meaning: Headphones read as personal listening, sound for one person rather than the room, which is why music apps and audio guides use them. A speaker means sound playing out loud, a music note means the content itself, and a headset with a microphone boom means talking as well as listening, usually support or gaming chat. Without a mic, this glyph leans towards listening.
uses: Music streaming app: marks the connected device chip when audio is playing through wireless headphones.
Museum guide app: opens the audio tour for an exhibit, with track numbers matching the gallery labels.
Help centre header: links to phone support, showing a person is ready to speak with the customer.
Video game settings: labels the sound output section with surround sound and voice chat volume options.
tips: For live support, add a microphone boom or a label like Talk to us, because plain headphones suggest listening rather than speaking.
Keep the ear cups chunky at 16 px; thin cups disappear and the headband alone looks like an arch or a magnet.
When it shows a connected device, include the device name in the label so screen readers announce where sound is going.

faq.q: What is the difference between a headphones icon and a headset icon?
faq.a: A headset adds a small microphone arm in front of the mouth, so it means speaking as well as listening. Use it for customer support, calls and gaming chat. Plain headphones mean listening only, which suits music, podcasts and audio guides.

faq.q: Why do support pages use headphones?
faq.a: Support pages use headphones because call centre staff wear them, so the glyph suggests a real person ready to help. If your support is chat only, a speech bubble is clearer, and the headphones can stay for phone or voice support options.
